title: Sable and the Current
premise: Yara Okafor, a nonbinary riverboat captain scraping by on cargo runs and an old debt to the ferry guild, discovers a drowned cave at low tide containing a compass that points not north but toward a person: their presumed-dead mother, who vanished twenty years ago chasing a legendary mountain pass called the Sable Current. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and joined by a runaway cartographer's apprentice named Teo and a disgraced guide named Marisol, Yara races across the range before the snows close the pass. At the summit they learn their mother is alive but dying, having spent two decades guarding the pass from the guild that wants to charge admission to it, and Yara must choose between saving her and saving the route for everyone who travels free. In the end Yara buries their mother at the pass, breaks the guild's claim with the compass as legal proof of inheritance, and returns to the river with a found family and a name that finally fits.
about_author: Ines Sterling is a former deckhand turned novelist who writes adventure stories about people who belong to water more than to land. They live in a converted tugboat with a stubborn dog and a library of unread nautical charts.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A routine cargo run down the Verre River establishes their competence, their debt to the ferry guild, and their careful, unglamorous life. Emotional beat: quiet restlessness beneath mastery.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Trouble
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. An unprecedented low tide exposes a cave mouth near Widow's Bend. Yara, unable to resist, rows in and finds a sealed chest bearing their mother's initials. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: The Compass That Lies
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The chest holds a strange brass compass whose needle ignores north and swings toward the mountains, plus a half-burned letter. Emotional beat: the past knocking loudly.

chapters.title: Guild Men at the Dock
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Guild enforcers arrive asking about salvage rights; their captain, Odile Voss, offers to buy the compass and makes clear refusal has a price. Emotional beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Teo Jumps Aboard
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. A cartographer's apprentice stows away on Yara's boat, fleeing Voss's employ, claiming he can read the letter's coded margins. Emotional beat: two loners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Letter Says
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Deciphered, the letter names the Sable Current, a free high pass, and a warning: 'Voss must never hold the needle.' Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as burden, not treasure.

chapters.title: Burning the Berth
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara sells the boat to cover the debt, severing their last tie to the river. Emotional beat: grief for a life chosen by necessity, not desire.

chapters.title: The Town That Charges Admission
chapters.summary: Yara and Teo's POV, alternating. They pass through a guild-controlled town where even the mountain view is ticketed. Emotional beat: anger crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Marisol the Disgraced
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A drunk ex-guide in a border saloon once led the expedition Yara's mother vanished on; she agrees to guide them for absolution, not coin. Emotional beat: shame offered a second chance.

chapters.title: First Ascent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The trio begins the climb; Yara's river instincts translate badly to scree and cold. Emotional beat: humility, and the first spark of trust.

chapters.title: The Needle Pulls
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The compass needle strengthens near a shrine cairn holding a second letter from Yara's mother, addressed to 'my child, whoever you become.' Emotional beat: being seen by the dead.

chapters.title: Voss on the Trail
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The guild captain follows with hired climbers, motivated by a debt of her own to the guild's founders. Emotional beat: antagonist given a human engine.

chapters.title: The Rope Bridge
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A crossing nearly kills Teo; Marisol freezes, haunted by the expedition where people died under her. Emotional beat: old failure resurfacing.

chapters.title: Yara Catches
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara saves Teo, and the three argue about whether the journey is worth dying for. Emotional beat: found family forged in friction.

chapters.title: Weather Turning
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. First snow falls weeks early; the pass window is shrinking. They find evidence Voss's party is a day behind. Emotional beat: the clock made visible.

chapters.title: The Hermit of the Ledges
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A hermit who once served Yara's mother shares supplies and a warning: the mother is alive, and has not wanted to be found. Emotional beat: hope and hurt in the same breath.

chapters.title: Yara's Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Around the fire, Yara tells Teo and Marisol about choosing the name Yara and the pronoun 'they.' Emotional beat: identity as self-made inheritance.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Voss's climbers ambush them; Marisol negotiates a stalemate by revealing she knows a hidden route Voss doesn't. Emotional beat: leverage earned from past sins.

chapters.title: The Hidden Route
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The secret path is brutal and beautiful; Marisol finally explains what happened on the fatal expedition, and that Yara's mother ordered the retreat that saved her. Emotional beat: guilt reframed.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Flashback: Voss grew up paying tolls, joined the guild to change it from within, and lost herself. She believes controlling the pass is the only way. Emotional beat: the villain's mirror.

chapters.title: The Needle Breaks
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The compass cracks in a fall; the needle still works but the casing, which holds a guild seal, is exposed, proving legal inheritance of the pass. Emotional beat: the treasure was the paper trail all along.

chapters.title: Storm Camp
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Trapped two days by a storm, the trio shares a meager birthday celebration for Teo. Emotional beat: warmth at altitude; family chosen, declared.

chapters.title: Betrayal of Convenience
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol secretly signals Voss's party, offering the hidden route in exchange for amnesty, then immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: fear outbidding loyalty.

chapters.title: The Icefall Crossing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A serac collapse splits the group; Teo and Yara take the high route, Marisol the low. Emotional beat: terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Teo's Map
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Teo admits he's been drafting a new map of the free route the whole way, to publish if they succeed. Emotional beat: each member contributing their own inheritance.

chapters.title: Marisol's Choice
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol misleads Voss into a dead-end chute at the cost of her amnesty. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with consequence.

chapters.title: The Sable Current
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach the pass: a wind-carved corridor where snow streams like a river. A small cabin stands at its heart. Emotional beat: awe, and the trembling before reunion.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Cabin
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara's mother, Adaeze, is alive, aged and ill, and greets them with a rifle raised before recognizing the compass. Emotional beat: twenty years collapsing into one breath.

chapters.title: Twenty Winters
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. She explains she faked her death to keep the guild from torturing her for the route, and has guarded it since. Emotional beat: love that chose distance as protection.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss reaches the pass with her remaining climbers and offers Adaeze a deal: legitimacy for control. Emotional beat: two weary women negotiating over a child's inheritance.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara produces the compass casing with the guild seal and Adaeze's letters: the pass was granted to their family in perpetuity, free for all travelers. Emotional beat: paper as weapon.

chapters.title: Voss's Counter
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss disputes the claim; her climbers waver, many having paid tolls all their lives. Emotional beat: an army discovering it agrees with the other side.

chapters.title: Adaeze Falters
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Adaeze collapses; her illness is advanced. She asks Yara to decide the pass's future. Emotional beat: inheritance handed over while the giver still breathes.

chapters.title: The Storm at the Summit
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A killer storm hits; Yara leads everyone, including Voss's climbers, into the cabin and the pass shelters them all. Emotional beat: the mountain itself testifying for the free road.

chapters.title: What Yara Decides
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara offers Voss a role: the pass stays free, but the guild funds its upkeep and Teo's map becomes the official chart. Emotional beat: victory as negotiation, not conquest.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Last Morning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Adaeze dies at dawn, at the pass she kept, with Yara holding her hand. Emotional beat: grief earned and clean.

chapters.title: The Burial Cairn
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They bury Adaeze at the summit; Marisol speaks the names of her old dead expedition alongside her. Emotional beat: mourning as unburdening.

chapters.title: Descent Before Winter
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The group races down the eastern slope ahead of the deep snows, carrying Adaeze's journals. Emotional beat: lightness after loss.

chapters.title: The Guild Reckoning
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Back in the lowlands, Voss presents the claim to the guild council; the tolls fall. She resigns, unburdened. Emotional beat: the antagonist released.

chapters.title: Sable and the Current
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara buys a new boat, names it Sable Current, and takes Teo and Marisol on as crew. The compass, repaired, points at nothing now, because there is no one left to find. Emotional beat: home rebuilt, wider than before.
